body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students add and subtract within 20 using making ten, doubles and near doubles, and the relationship between addition and subtraction (1.OA.C.6).
- Students apply properties of operations as strategies: changing the order of addends, and grouping three addends to make a ten (1.OA.B.3).
- Students understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem (1.OA.B.4) and find the unknown number in an equation (1.OA.D.8).
- Students understand the equal sign and decide whether equations are true or false (1.OA.D.7).
- Students solve word problems with three addends (1.OA.A.2) and with a start or change unknown (1.OA.A.1).

MATERIALS
- Two ten frames per student and two colors of counters
- Number bond mats (a whole and two parts)
- A balance scale or a drawn balance, for showing that both sides of the equal sign are the same
- Fact family triangle cards
- Tablets with the class activities open, for photos of work

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read Smart Ways to Add and Subtract together. Lesson activity: Make a Ten. Model 9 + 4 on two ten frames: slide one counter to fill the first frame. Students solve the questions with counters and explain one to a partner.
Day 2: Doubles and near doubles: build 6 + 6 and 6 + 7 with cubes. Then number bonds: show 4 and 7 make 11, and write all four facts. Students start Fact Families and Missing Numbers.
Day 3: Finish Fact Families and Missing Numbers. Talk through the shell story: what do we know, and what is missing? Show it as ? + 5 = 13.
Day 4: The equal sign means "is the same as". Use the balance: is 4 + 1 the same as 5 + 2? Students complete True or False?, looking for a ten in three-number problems.
Day 5: Assessment: Strategies Check. Read each problem aloud. Students may use ten frames. Ask a few students to explain their strategy for problem 2 aloud.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: work within 10 first (fact families for 3, 4, 7), and keep ten frames and counters out for every problem.
- Support: for missing-number problems, cover part of a group of counters with a cup and ask how many are hiding.
- Stretch: ask for two different strategies for 8 + 7 and which is faster; write equations with numbers on both sides (8 + 5 = ? + 6) and true-or-false problems for a partner.
- Multilingual learners: teach "same as", "missing", "true" and "false" with the balance and gestures (thumbs up, thumbs down). Keep the strategy names on an anchor chart with a picture for each.
- Watch for students who read = as "the answer is". When they say 7 = 8 - 1 is false "because the answer goes last", return to the balance.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
We are learning smart ways to add and subtract, such as making a ten (9 + 4 is the same as 10 + 3) and using doubles (if 6 + 6 = 12, then 6 + 7 = 13). Ask your child to show you their favorite strategy. Play "how many are hiding": put 12 spoons on the table, hide some under a towel, and ask how many are hiding if 5 are showing.
title: Teacher guide: Adding and Subtracting Strategies
